slides.say: For every three numbers x, y and z, diamond of x, y, z is equal to x to the power of y z, plus y to the power of x z, plus z to the power of x y. Diamond of one, one, and diamond of two, one, four, is equal to what?
A brand-new operation, but only numbers, no unknowns. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, the standard way, and then a sharp shortcut.
[short pause] The diamond appears twice, so we run it twice, and always the inner one first. x is two, y is one, and z is four. Each number goes to the power of the product of the other two.
at: x is two, y is one

slides.say: One times four is four, and two to the fourth is sixteen. Two times four is eight, and one to the eighth is one. Two times one is two, and four squared is sixteen. Thirty-three.

Now the outer one, one, one, thirty-three. One to any power is one, twice. One times one is one, and thirty-three to the first is thirty-three. One plus one plus thirty-three is thirty-five. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] And a shortcut. What's different? We look at the outer diamond before calculating anything. Sometimes a zero there makes the inner value irrelevant. Say the outer call were the inner value, zero, one. The inner value to the power zero is one, zero to a positive power is zero, and one to any power is one. Two, whatever is inside.

Here there's no zero, but the two ones do something similar. One to any power, twice, and the last number to the power of one times one stays itself. So the outer diamond is two plus whatever is in the third slot.
Two plus thirty-three is thirty-five. Choice number three. Shorter, if you spot it under pressure. If not, the first way always works. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
